title: Invited to Hawaii with C. P. Johnson's band
summary: After a Granz tour and Berg's, he joined Gerald Wilson's friends in C. P. Johnson's band for six weeks in Hawaii with Red Callender and Dexter Gordon.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Earlier today on the way to rehearsal, Red Callender was, that
You mentioned (inaudible). The first time you worked with Red Calendar was in Hawaii?
We went to Hawaii together for a year.
Everyone went to Hawaii. It was with
Red Calendar. What was it you were playing? You mentioned Dexter Gordon.
Yeah, Dexter was on the band, Red Calendar, myself. The guy who had the band was a drummer, and he couldn't drum very well, but he had the gig, you know. It was his job.

His name was C. P. Johnson. And this was in -- I tell you when -- I know exactly when this happened. This was about '47, because I was working with Norman Granz, and the tour ended up in the dead of winter in Toledo, Ohio, and it was so cold; at the end of every tour, Norman would ask us where did we want to go, and we started to -- New York.

So I told him I wanted to go to California, you know, and to get out of that cold weather. And Roy was coming out in California at that time. I think I mentioned this to you the other day. Roy Eldridge, he had a gig, Billy Berg's -- did I tell you about that?

Well, we spoke about that probably. Anyway, after that gig ended, this band was rehearsing to go to Hawaii for six weeks, and it was C. P. Johnson. He had the job. Gerald Wilson was rehearsing on trumpet, and Gerald called me about going. He says, come on and go. He says, a guy who's supposed to go, the trombone player, his name was Bedsel. He said, he has exams. He was studying to be a dentist, and he
had exams, and he said, just six weeks. Come on and go.

So I rehearsed with them a few days, and the -- Ulysses Livingston was the guitar player, and Preston -- what was Preston's name? He's a trumpet player. Eddie Preston, a trumpet player, and we all went over there and -- together, about six or seven of us.
